name: Set 6: Highveld Hustle
description: Cricket Centuries, 90s Grunge, Fast Food Empires & Ancient Wonders

questions.q: How many cards are in a standard deck of playing cards (excluding jokers)?
questions.fact: 4 suits of 13 cards each = 52 cards.

questions.q: What color is the gemstone known as an emerald?
questions.fact: Emeralds are a green variety of beryl.

questions.q: In bowling, what term describes scoring three consecutive strikes in a row?
questions.fact: A turkey: three strikes in a row.

questions.q: What South African fast-food brand is famous for the flame-grilled 'King Steer Burger' and seasoned hand-cut slap chips?
questions.fact: Founded in 1960 by George Halamandaris.

questions.q: Which mammal is the only one capable of true, sustained flight?
questions.fact: Bats possess webbed wings for true powered flight.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Spain?
questions.fact: Madrid, located in the geographical center of Spain.

questions.q: How many meters is a standard Olympic swimming pool in length?
questions.fact: 50 meters in length (long course).

questions.q: What popular breakfast egg dish, baked over a tomato and onion spicy sauce in a pan, is known as 'Shakshuka'?
answers: Poached eggs in spicy tomato relish
questions.fact: Middle Eastern and North African dish of eggs gently poached in spiced tomato sauce.

questions.q: What is the common name for the voice box in the human neck containing the vocal cords?
questions.fact: The larynx houses the vocal folds.

questions.q: Which South African television soap opera set around the mining town of The Deep aired for over two decades on SABC3?
questions.fact: Isidingo: The Need (1998-2020), set at the Horizon Deep mine.

questions.q: In the famous '438 Game' at the Wanderers in 2006, South Africa chased down Australia's 434. Who hit the winning boundary four over mid-off?
questions.fact: Mark Boucher lofted Brett Lee for four to seal the highest successful ODI run chase in history (438/9).

questions.q: Who scored an astonishing 175 off 111 balls for South Africa in that exact same 438 game?
questions.fact: Herschelle Gibbs played one of the most explosive one-day innings ever witnessed.

questions.q: Which South African cricket superstar holds the world record for the fastest ever ODI century, reaching 100 off just 31 balls against the West Indies?
questions.fact: AB de Villiers: 149 off 44 balls at the Wanderers on 18 January 2015.

questions.q: Which Springbok lock forward, famous for dominating the lineouts, was named Man of the Match in the 2007 Rugby World Cup Final?
questions.fact: Victor Matfield's mastery of the lineout choked England's possession throughout the final.

questions.q: Who was the legendary South African cricket captain who famously batted with a broken hand at the SCG against Australia in 2009?
questions.fact: Graeme Smith walked out to bat at number 11 with a broken left hand and damaged elbow to try and save the Test.

questions.q: In tennis, what Grand Slam tournament is played on traditional grass courts in London every July?
questions.fact: The Championships, Wimbledon: the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

questions.q: Which South African rugby prop was nicknamed 'The Beast' by roaring crowds at Kings Park and around the world?
questions.fact: 'BEEEEAAAST!' 117 caps and 2019 World Cup champion.

questions.q: What is the maximum break of points possible in a standard frame of snooker without fouls?
questions.fact: 15 reds with 15 blacks (120 points) plus the 6 colors (27 points) = 147.

questions.q: Which South African long jumper won the Olympic silver medal in Beijing 2008 and world gold in Berlin 2009?
questions.fact: Khotso Mokoena won South Africa's only medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

questions.q: In rugby league or union, how many points are awarded for an unconverted try in modern rugby union?
questions.fact: Raised from 4 points to 5 points in 1992.

questions.q: Which Seattle grunge band released the genre-defining 1991 album Nevermind, featuring 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'?
questions.fact: Fronted by Kurt Cobain, with Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl.

questions.q: Which multi-racial South African band fronted by Claire Johnston had massive 1989/1990 hits with 'Special Star' and 'Dance Some More'?
questions.fact: Mango Groove blended big band swing, marabi, and kwela pop.

questions.q: What British rock band brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher led during the Britpop era with hits like 'Wonderwall' and 'Don't Look Back in Anger'?
questions.fact: Their 1995 album (What's the Story) Morning Glory? sold over 22 million copies.

questions.q: Which pop diva sang the mega-selling theme song 'My Heart Will Go On' for the movie Titanic?
questions.fact: Composed by James Horner, winning the Oscar for Best Original Song.

questions.q: What Swedish pop duo consisting of Marie Fredriksson and Per Gessle scored monster hits with 'It Must Have Been Love' and 'Joyride'?
questions.fact: Roxette had four US Billboard number-one singles.

questions.q: Which American hip hop group released the 1992 dance party anthem 'Jump Around'?
questions.fact: Produced by DJ Muggs.

questions.q: In 1994, which American punk rock trio released the smash hit album Dookie featuring 'Basket Case'?
questions.fact: Billie Joe Armstrong, Mike Dirnt, and Tré Cool.

questions.q: Which South African band had a giant hit in 1987 with the anti-conscription ballad 'Weeping', featuring the melody of 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika'?
questions.fact: Written by Dan Heymann, featuring Basil Coetzee on saxophone.

questions.q: Who released the hit 1999 Latin pop anthem 'Livin' la Vida Loca'?
questions.fact: Ignited the global Latin pop explosion.

questions.q: Which American rock band fronted by Anthony Kiedis and Flea released the 1991 hit album Blood Sugar Sex Magik containing 'Under the Bridge'?
questions.fact: Produced by Rick Rubin.

questions.q: Which South African family steakhouse franchise is famous for its Native American-themed decor, kids' play areas, and signature basting sauce?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Founded by Allen Ambor in Newlands, Cape Town in 1967.

questions.q: What is the famous secret ingredient blend count famously advertised on Colonel Sanders' Kentucky Fried Chicken recipe?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: The Colonel's secret blend of 11 herbs and spices kept in a safe in Louisville, Kentucky.

questions.q: What spicy Portuguese-style chicken franchise was founded in Rosettenville, Johannesburg in 1987 by Fernando Duarte and Robbie Brozin?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Named after Fernando's son Nando; now operating in over 30 countries.

questions.q: What is the distinctive bread bun used in South African cuisine that is deep-fried from yeasted dough and often filled with curried mince?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Crispy golden outside, soft steamy dough inside, stuffed with curried mince.

questions.q: Which cut of beef, famous in South American churrasco and increasingly popular at SA braais, has a thick fat cap and is called the rump cap?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Picanha (sirloin cap / rump cap): seasoned with coarse rock salt and skewered over coals.

questions.q: In a bar, what non-alcoholic cocktail made with ginger ale, a dash of grenadine, and a maraschino cherry is named after a child movie star?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Invented at Chasen's in Beverly Hills for the young actress.

questions.q: What is the primary flavor profile of the classic South African liqueur Van Der Hum?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Van Der Hum is flavored with Cape naartjie peels, brandy, and spices.

questions.q: What popular burger topping consists of thinly sliced beef cured and dried, crumbled over the melted cheese?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: The biltong burger: a pub classic across South Africa.

questions.q: Which Mexican distilled spirit must be produced specifically within the Mexican state of Jalisco and designated regions, unlike general Mezcal?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: All Tequilas are Mezcals, but only those made from blue agave in Jalisco (and limited municipalities) are Tequila.

questions.q: What famous brand of hot sauce originated on Avery Island, Louisiana, and is aged in white oak whiskey barrels?
questions.round: Round 4 · Fast Food Empires & Secret Recipes
questions.fact: Created by Edmund McIlhenny in 1868.

questions.q: Which of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is the only one that still largely stands intact today?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Built around 2560 BC for Pharaoh Khufu; survived for over 4,500 years.

questions.q: Approximately how old are the rocks that make up Table Mountain in Cape Town?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Table Mountain's sandstone and granite base dates back over 500-600 million years, making it six times older than the Himalayas.

questions.q: In which city stands the colossal Roman amphitheater known as the Colosseum, completed in 80 AD?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: The Flavian Amphitheatre, capable of holding up to 80,000 spectators.

questions.q: What is the deepest known location in the world's oceans, plunging nearly 11,000 meters down in the western Pacific?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Challenger Deep reaches approximately 10,994 meters below sea level.

questions.q: Which ivory-white marble mausoleum on the Yamuna river in Agra, India was commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Built to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.q: What is the longest river in the world by traditional geographic consensus?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Flowing roughly 6,650 km through northeastern Africa.

questions.q: In which South American country would you find the ancient Incan citadel of Machu Picchu perched high in the Andes?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Built around 1450 AD above the Sacred Valley.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Germany, reunited after the fall of the Wall in 1989?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Berlin is the largest city in Germany by population and area.

questions.q: What colossal suspension bridge in San Francisco, painted in 'International Orange', opened to traffic in 1937?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Spans the Golden Gate strait connecting San Francisco to Marin County.

questions.q: Which South African coastal road boasts the world's highest commercial bungee jump located at Bloukrans Bridge?
questions.round: Round 5 · Wonders of the Ancient & Modern World
questions.fact: Bloukrans Bridge Bungee: 216 meters above the Bloukrans River on the N2.

questions.q: How many total runs were scored by both teams combined in the historic 438 cricket match between Australia and South Africa at the Wanderers in 2006?
questions.fact: Australia 434 + South Africa 438 = 872 runs in 99.5 overs.

questions.q: How many meters high is the Bloukrans Bridge bungee jump above the river?
questions.fact: 216 meters (709 feet).

questions.q: In what calendar year did AB de Villiers score his 31-ball world record century against the West Indies at the Wanderers?
questions.fact: 18 January 2015.
